Question Paper  
Exam Date & Time: 24-Nov-2025 (02:00 PM - 05:00 PM)  
  
  
  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
  FIFTH SEMESTER B.TECH. DEGREE EXAMINATIONS - NOVEMBER 2025  
  SUBJECT: ICT 3123/IT_3123 SOFTWARE ENGINEERING  
  (SPL: INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY)  
  SOFTWARE ENGINEERING [ICT 3123]  
Marks: 50                                                                                                     Duration: 180 mins.  
  
  A  
Answer all the questions.  
  
1A)               A university wants to automate its online course registration system. The system allows students to (5)  
  log in, view available courses, register for new courses, and receive confirmation messages upon  
  successful registration. The system also checks for prerequisites and seat availability before  
  confirming enrollment.  
  Design a detailed Sequence Diagram for the course registration process described above, clearly  
  showing the interaction among objects such as Student, CourseCatalog, RegistrationSystem, and  
  Database. Ensure your diagram reflects message order, conditional checks, and system  
  responses.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Create"  
  
1B)               A software development team is designing an online payment gateway that interacts with multiple        (3)  
  external modules-such as User Authentication, Order Processing, Transaction Handler, and  
  Notification Service. During design review, it is observed that changes in one module often require  
  modifications in several others, causing high maintenance effort.  
  Analyze the design of this system to identify the type of coupling exhibited among its modules.  
  Explain how this level of coupling affects system maintainability and propose one improvement to  
  reduce coupling.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
1C)               Differentiate between unit testing, integration testing, and system testing strategies. Explain when   (2)  
  each should be applied in the software development lifecycle.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
2A)               An organization is creating an e-commerce application architecture that integrates inventory           (5)  
  management, user authentication, payment services, and customer notifications. During system  
  design, the architect must decide how different components will interact and how the system will  
  handle both dynamic content and performance optimization.  
  Analyze the system requirements and determine suitable architectural views (logical, process, and  
  deployment) for this application. Explain how these views help in addressing system performance  
  and integration challenges.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
2B)               An online food delivery system allows users to:                                                        (3)  
  • Begin in the Order Browsing state.  
  • Move to Order Placed after confirming the selection.  
  Page #1

• Transition to Preparing Order, then Out for Delivery, and finally Delivered.  
  • A user can Cancel before the order is prepared, returning to Order Browsing.  
  Construct a UML State Transition Diagram illustrating the order life cycle in the food delivery  
  system. Include states, events, and transitions, ensuring all conditional paths are represented.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Create"  
  
2C)   In a student management system, the "StudentModule" performs different tasks such as adding            (2)  
  student details, generating reports, and calculating exam grades.  
  Analyze whether this module has high or low cohesion and explain your answer briefly.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
3A)   Consider the following code segment:                                                                   (5)  
  
  
  Construct the Control Flow Graph (CFG) for this code segment and calculate the cyclomatic  
  complexity using all methods. Design a comprehensive set of test cases that achieve basis path  
  coverage. Justify how your testcases ensure thorough testing of all independent paths.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Create"  
  
3B)   A software project faces the following risks: 70% probability of key developer leaving (cost impact:   (3)  
  \$12,000), 40% probability of requirement changes (cost impact: \$8,000), and 25% probability of  
  technology integration issues (cost impact: \$20,000).  
  Page #2

Analyze these risks by calculating risk exposure for each using the Risk Exposure formula. Develop  
  a comprehensive RMMM (Risk Mitigation, Monitoring, and Management) strategy for the highest  
  priority risk, including specific mitigation steps, monitoring indicators, and contingency plans.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
3C)   Distinguish between functional and non-functional requirements in software engineering. Analyze      (2)  
  how proper requirements specification impacts software design and testing phases with relevant  
  examples.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
4A)   A password validation system has the following requirements:                                         (5)  
  • Password length: 8-20 characters  
  • Must contain at least one uppercase letter  
  • Must contain at least one lowercase letter  
  • Must contain at least one digit  
  • Must contain at least one special character (!@#\$%^&*)  
  • Cannot contain spaces  
  • Cannot be identical to the last 5 passwords  
  Apply equivalence class partitioning and boundary value analysis techniques to design a  
  comprehensive test suite for this password validation system. Create test cases for both valid and  
  invalid equivalence classes, identify boundary values for the length constraint, and evaluate how  
  your test cases achieve maximum coverage with minimum redundancy.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Create"  
  
4B)   An e-learning platform allows students to enroll in courses, submit assignments, take quizzes, and   (3)  
  track progress. The system involves actors: Student, Instructor, and Administrator. Develop a  
  comprehensive use case model for this e-learning system that includes at least 5 major use cases  
  with proper relationships. Create an activity diagram for the "Submit Assignment" use case that  
  shows the complete workflow including validation steps and error handling.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Create"  
  
4C)   Compare Agile methodology with Unified Process (UP) in terms of their approach to requirements       (2)  
  handling, iteration management, and risk management. Analyze the scenarios where each  
  methodology would be most appropriate.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
5A)   A library management system manages books, members, authors, and transactions. The system            (5)  
  tracks book borrowing, returns, reservations, and member information. Consider the following  
  relationships: a book can have multiple authors, a member can borrow multiple books, books can  
  be reserved by multiple members, and the system maintains borrowing history.  
  Design a comprehensive class diagram for this library management system that includes at least 5  
  classes with appropriate attributes, methods, and relationships with multiplicities.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Create"  
  
5B)   Analyze the role of Software Configuration Management in coordinating team-based software            (3)  
  development. Evaluate how version control, baseline management, and change control contribute  
  to project success.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
5C)   Differentiate between Aspect-Oriented Software Development and Formal process models.                (2)  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  
  Page #3
